request.input:
You repair a Boolean network model of the DNA damage response (a published model, Gupta et al. 2023).
A claim read from the literature was turned into a rule change by a fixed template, and an exact solver rejected the
change: the edited network contradicts behaviours the model must keep (the verification cases). Propose another rule
for the node that still expresses the claim but passes those cases.

Rules are written with node names and the operators ! (not), & (and), | (or) and parentheses. A node is 1 when active.
DNA_damage is the only input. These are the nodes you may use: AKT, AMPK_MAPK, ATM_pH2AX, ATR, BAX, BCL2, CHK1, CHK2, Caspase, Cdc25, Cdc2_CycB, DNA_PK, DNA_damage, E2F1, Mdm2, Myc, PTEN, PUMA, RB, Sirt1, TUG1, ULK1_Beclin1, WWP1, Wee1, Wip1, hTERT, mTORC1, mTORC2, miR221, p21, p53, p53_A, p53_INP1, p53_K

CLAIM: CHK1 inhibits Cdc25   (6 paper(s))
EVIDENCE:
- PMC2243162 (review statement of checkpoint pathways): "Checkpoint kinase-2 and Chk1 inactivate CDC25 phosphatases, culminating in cell cycle arrest."
- PMC2243162 (at G2 after DNA damage in G2 or escape from earlier checkpoints): "At G2, Chk1 is activated by ATR to phosphorylate CDC25A, -B, and -C (Boutros, 2006), preventing cyclin B/CDK1 activation and resulting in G2 arrest."
- PMC3631220 (review statement cited from other work, upon DDR): "Upon to DDR, Chk1 is activated and inhibits the activation of the downstream target of Cdc25C, resulted in the downregulation of cyclinB1/Cdc2 kinase [57]."
- PMC3913755 (review statement citing prior work): "Cdc25 can be phosphorylated by Chk1/Chk2 on Ser-323 (Cdc25B) and Ser-216 (Cdc25C) and functionally inactivated by binding to 14-3-3 proteins [26]–[28]."

NODE TO CHANGE: Cdc25
CURRENT RULE:   Cdc25, (!ATM_pH2AX | !AMPK_MAPK) & !Wee1 & !PTEN
TEMPLATE RULE (rejected): Cdc25, ((!ATM_pH2AX | !AMPK_MAPK) & !Wee1 & !PTEN) & !CHK1

WHY IT WAS REJECTED (counterexamples from the solver; "setting" fixes nodes to 0 or 1, a phenotype is read from the
fixed points; the witness is a fixed point of the edited network):
- V04 (Figure 3, TUG1 KO); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'TUG1': 0}: unexpected; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 1, 'AMPK_MAPK': 0, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'Wee1': 0, 'PTEN': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0, 'CHK1': 1}
- V05 (Figure 3, miR-221 E1); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'miR221': 1}: unexpected; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 1, 'AMPK_MAPK': 0, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'Wee1': 0, 'PTEN': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0, 'CHK1': 1}
- V06 (Figure 3, miR-221 E1 + TUG1 KO); setting {'DNA_damage': 1, 'miR221': 1, 'TUG1': 0}: unexpected; expected phenotypes ['apoptosis'] (exact), found ['apoptosis', 'senescence']; witness fixed point {'ATM_pH2AX': 1, 'AMPK_MAPK': 0, 'p53': 1, 'p53_A': 1, 'p53_K': 0, 'p21': 1, 'Wip1': 1, 'Cdc25': 0, 'Cdc2_CycB': 0, 'Wee1': 0, 'PTEN': 0, 'mTORC1': 1, 'mTORC2': 1, 'ULK1_Beclin1': 0, 'BAX': 0, 'Caspase': 0, 'CHK1': 1}

Requirements, all checked by the solver afterwards:
- CHK1 must be able to switch Cdc25 off and never on: it acts on Cdc25 only in the direction 'inhibits'.
- Keep every influence the current rule has: every node in the current rule must still affect the new rule in the same way.
- Use only the nodes listed above. Do not use Cdc25 in its own rule.
- You may restrict WHEN the claimed effect applies by combining it with other nodes, if the evidence context (cell
  type, condition) or the counterexample suggests a condition. Say which condition you chose and why. Do not invent a
  mechanism the evidence does not support.
- If no rule can both express the claim and pass the cases, set give_up to true and explain.

Answer as JSON: {"rule": "<expression only, no node name and no comma>", "explanation": "...", "give_up": false}.

text: {"explanation": "Kept base (!ATM_pH2AX | !AMPK_MAPK) & !Wee1 & !PTEN and restricted CHK1 inhibition to AMPK_MAPK-active contexts: !(CHK1 & AMPK_MAPK) = (!CHK1 | !AMPK_MAPK). Condition suggested by counterexamples V04-V06 which all have AMPK_MAPK=0, ATM_pH2AX=1, Wee1=0, PTEN=0, CHK1=1 where Cdc25 must stay 1 to keep apoptosis-only; template incorrectly forces 0. With restriction, witness gives 1, rescuing cases, while CHK1 can still switch Cdc25 1->0 when base=1 and AMPK_MAPK=1 (e.g. ATM=0, AMPK=1). No new regulator introduced, only refinement of existing regulators, so no new mechanism invented. CHK1 only inhibits, all original influences remain inhibitory.", "give_up": false, "rule": "((!ATM_pH2AX | !AMPK_MAPK) & !Wee1 & !PTEN) & (!CHK1 | !AMPK_MAPK)"}
